message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to traffic coming from the right. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing on either side. | | **Headlights** | • Must be used from sunset to sunrise, or when visibility is reduced. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Only authorized towing companies may tow vehicles.
• Private towing is prohibited unless the vehicle is abandoned. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses automated enforcement; violations result in tickets. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (except some exempt categories). | | **Special Rules for Motorcycles** | • Must have a helmet (unless under 18).
• Must use a motorcycle‑specific license endorsement. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | | **Roadside Assistance & Tow‑away** | • Texas law allows towing of abandoned vehicles but not for private towing. | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official rules and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text. - **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances (e.g., city speed limits). Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular rule or how to handle a specific situation!
